title: DSSSB English Language & Comprehension - Reading Comprehension Practice Test

questions.q:
Passage 1: Education is not merely the acquisition of knowledge or technical skills; it is the harmonious development of physical, mental, and moral faculties of an individual. True education empowers a person to distinguish between right and wrong, fosters critical thinking, and prepares one to face life's challenges with resilience. In modern times, the emphasis has shifted heavily toward academic scores and professional training, often neglecting character building and empathy. To build a balanced society, educational institutions must reintegrate value education alongside scientific and technical instruction.

According to the passage, what is the primary goal of true education?
options: Harmonious development of physical, mental, and moral faculties
Solely acquiring technical skills and academic degrees
Achieving top academic scores in competitive exams
Securing high-paying jobs in modern industries

questions.q: Passage 1 (Contd.): What aspect of education is often neglected in modern times according to the passage?
Passage 1 (Contd.): What does true education empower an individual to do?
Passage 1 (Contd.): What recommendation does the author give for building a balanced society?
options: Reintegrate value education with scientific and technical instruction
Focus only on moral education and ignore science
Increase the duration of academic examinations

questions.q: Passage 1 (Contd.): What is the synonym of the word 'resilience' as used in the passage context?

Passage 2: Environmental degradation is one of the most pressing crises facing humanity today. Deforestation, industrial pollution, and unsustainable resource consumption have led to severe climate anomalies, biodiversity loss, and ecological imbalance. While global conventions continuously negotiate carbon reduction targets, meaningful change requires grassroots initiatives and individual responsibility. Adopting sustainable lifestyles, reducing plastic consumption, and planting trees are simple yet effective actions that every citizen can undertake to mitigate environmental harm.

What is identified as one of the most pressing crises facing humanity today?
Passage 2 (Contd.): What has directly led to severe climate anomalies and biodiversity loss?
options: Grassroots initiatives and tree planting drives
Reduction in plastic consumption by citizens

questions.q: Passage 2 (Contd.): According to the author, what is necessary alongside global conventions to achieve meaningful change?
Passage 2 (Contd.): Which of the following is mentioned as a simple action individuals can take?
Passage 2 (Contd.): What does the word 'mitigate' mean in the context of the passage?
options: To lessen or reduce the severity of

Passage 3: The digital revolution has fundamentally reshaped human communication, work, and daily life. The internet and social media platforms have democratized information access, enabling instant connection across geographical boundaries. However, this rapid technological advancement brings significant challenges, including cyber threats, spread of misinformation, and digital addiction. Excessive screen time and online engagement have also been linked to psychological stress and reduced face-to-face social interaction. Therefore, cultivating digital literacy and mindful usage is essential to harness technology positively.

How has the digital revolution impacted human life?
options: By reshaping communication, work, and daily life
By restricting global access to information
By eliminating the need for literacy

questions.q: Passage 3 (Contd.): What major benefit of internet and social media is highlighted in the text?
options: Preventing the spread of fake news
Reducing the need for digital devices

questions.q: Passage 3 (Contd.): Which of the following is cited as a negative consequence of excessive screen time?
options: Psychological stress and reduced face-to-face interaction
Improved social connections in real life

questions.q: Passage 3 (Contd.): What is required to harness technology positively according to the passage?
options: Cultivating digital literacy and mindful usage

questions.q: Passage 3 (Contd.): What is the antonym of 'democratized' as implied in the passage context?

Passage 4: Reading habit is one of the most enriching qualities a person can foster. It not only expands vocabulary and improves language proficiency but also enhances cognitive function and imagination. Books serve as gateways to diverse cultures, historical eras, and philosophical thought, broadening one's worldview. In an age dominated by short-form digital content, maintaining a deep reading habit requires conscious discipline. Fostering a love for reading from early childhood lays a solid foundation for lifelong learning and intellectual curiosity.

What is one primary benefit of developing a reading habit?
options: Expands vocabulary and improves language proficiency
Promotes reliance on short-form digital content
Limits one's understanding of global cultures

questions.q: Passage 4 (Contd.): How do books help in broadening an individual's worldview?
options: By acting as gateways to diverse cultures and historical eras
By restricting reading to short-form content
By eliminating the need for discipline
By focusing solely on technical grammar rules

questions.q: Passage 4 (Contd.): What makes maintaining a deep reading habit challenging today?
options: Availability of too many physical books

questions.q: Passage 4 (Contd.): Why is it important to cultivate reading habits from early childhood?
options: It lays a solid foundation for lifelong learning
It prevents children from attending school
It reduces the need for critical thinking

questions.q: Passage 4 (Contd.): Choose the word closest in meaning to 'foster':

Passage 5: Time management is an essential life skill for achieving personal and professional success. It involves prioritizing tasks, setting realistic goals, and avoiding procrastination. People who manage their time effectively experience lower stress levels, higher productivity, and a better work-life balance. Conversely, poor time management often leads to missed deadlines, sub-par performance, and chronic burnout. Utilizing planners, prioritizing urgent and important tasks, and learning to say no to non-essential activities are key strategies for effective time control.

What are key components of effective time management according to the text?
options: Prioritizing tasks and setting realistic goals
Taking on all non-essential tasks simultaneously
Working continuously without taking any breaks

questions.q: Passage 5 (Contd.): What is a direct outcome of managing time effectively?
options: Lower stress levels and higher productivity

questions.q: Passage 5 (Contd.): What is a major consequence of poor time management?
Passage 5 (Contd.): Which strategy is suggested to maintain time control?
options: Learning to say no to non-essential activities
Avoiding the use of daily planners
Delaying urgent tasks until deadlines pass

questions.q: Passage 5 (Contd.): What is the antonym of 'procrastination'?

Passage 6: Healthy eating habits are fundamental to maintaining overall physical well-being and longevity. A balanced diet rich in whole grains, fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and healthy fats provides essential nutrients that power metabolic functions and bolster immunity. Conversely, excessive consumption of processed foods high in refined sugars and unhealthy fats contributes to obesity, cardiovascular diseases, and diabetes. Developing nutritional awareness and making conscious dietary choices are critical steps toward preventing chronic health conditions.

What constitutes a balanced diet according to the passage?
options: Whole grains, fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and healthy fats
Processed foods high in refined sugars and fats
High intake of fast foods and aerated drinks

questions.q: Passage 6 (Contd.): What health issues are linked to excessive processed food intake?
Passage 6 (Contd.): Why are essential nutrients vital for the human body?
options: They power metabolic functions and bolster immunity
They increase reliance on medical treatments

questions.q: Passage 6 (Contd.): What step is necessary to prevent chronic health conditions?
options: Developing nutritional awareness and conscious dietary choices
Eliminating all fats and carbohydrates completely

questions.q: Passage 6 (Contd.): What is the synonym of 'bolster' as used in the passage?

Passage 7: Yoga is an ancient Indian discipline that integrates physical postures, breath control, and meditation to promote holistic health. Unlike conventional physical exercises that focus primarily on muscular strength, yoga emphasizes mind-body harmony and inner tranquility. Regular practice of yoga reduces stress levels, improves body flexibility, enhances respiratory efficiency, and boosts mental clarity. In today's fast-paced urban life, yoga offers a practical pathway to achieve mental peace and physical vitality.

What distinguishes yoga from conventional physical exercises?
options: It emphasizes mind-body harmony and inner tranquility
It focuses solely on building muscular strength
It ignores physical postures and flexibility
It requires complex machinery to practice

questions.q: Passage 7 (Contd.): What are the core components of yoga mentioned in the passage?
options: Physical postures, breath control, and meditation

questions.q: Passage 7 (Contd.): Which of the following is a physical benefit of regular yoga practice?
options: Improved body flexibility and respiratory efficiency

questions.q: Passage 7 (Contd.): Why is yoga considered particularly valuable in modern times?
options: It offers a pathway to mental peace in fast-paced urban life
It eliminates the need for proper nutrition

questions.q: Passage 7 (Contd.): Give the meaning of 'tranquility' in the context of the text:

Passage 8: Water conservation is an urgent global imperative as climate change and population growth strain freshwater supplies. Agriculture accounts for the majority of global freshwater consumption, making efficient irrigation techniques like drip and sprinkler systems vital. Furthermore, urban rainwater harvesting, industrial water recycling, and public awareness campaigns are essential components of sustainable water management. Without immediate conservation efforts, severe water scarcity threatens food security, economic stability, and human survival in many regions.

Which sector consumes the majority of global freshwater supplies?
Passage 8 (Contd.): What efficient irrigation techniques are recommended in the text?
Passage 8 (Contd.): What factors are straining global freshwater supplies?
Passage 8 (Contd.): What could be a severe threat if water conservation is ignored?
options: Threat to food security and economic stability

questions.q: Passage 8 (Contd.): Find the synonym for 'imperative':

Passage 9: Renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power, are vital for transitioning away from fossil fuels. Burning coal, oil, and natural gas releases greenhouse gases that drive global warming and atmospheric pollution. Solar panels and wind turbines harness natural, clean energy without emitting carbon dioxide during power generation. Although initial infrastructure costs remain relatively high, rapid technological advancements and economies of scale are making renewable energy increasingly affordable and accessible globally.

Why is transitioning to renewable energy sources considered vital?
options: To reduce reliance on fossil fuels that emit greenhouse gases
To increase carbon dioxide emissions worldwide
To make power generation completely manual
To exhaust natural fossil fuel reserves faster

questions.q: Passage 9 (Contd.): What advantage do solar panels and wind turbines possess during energy generation?
options: They rely heavily on burning coal
They consume vast amounts of natural gas

questions.q: Passage 9 (Contd.): What initial obstacle is associated with renewable energy adoption?
options: Lack of solar radiation and wind energy

questions.q: Passage 9 (Contd.): What is making renewable energy more affordable over time?
options: Technological advancements and economies of scale
Higher taxes on clean energy generation

questions.q: Passage 9 (Contd.): What is the opposite of 'renewable' in the given context?

Passage 10: Biodiversity is the foundation of ecosystem stability and human survival. Forests, wetlands, oceans, and grasslands provide essential ecosystem services, including air purification, soil fertility, crop pollination, and climate regulation. Human activities like urbanization, industrial agriculture, and habitat destruction have accelerated species extinction at an alarming rate. Protecting natural habitats, enforcing conservation laws, and restoring degraded ecosystems are essential to preserve the delicate balance of life on Earth.

Why is biodiversity crucial for planet Earth?
options: It forms the foundation of ecosystem stability and human survival
It accelerates urbanization and land clearing
It eliminates natural wetlands and forests

questions.q: Passage 10 (Contd.): Which ecosystem service is mentioned in the passage?
Passage 10 (Contd.): Which human activity has accelerated species extinction?
Passage 10 (Contd.): What action is required to preserve Earth's delicate balance of life?
options: Protecting natural habitats and restoring ecosystems
Clearing remaining forest areas for housing

questions.q: Passage 10 (Contd.): Select the synonym of 'preserve' as used in the passage:

Passage 11: Financial literacy is the ability to understand and effectively use various financial skills, including personal financial management, budgeting, and investing. Lacking financial literacy leads to poor spending decisions, unmanageable debt, and lack of long-term security. Educating youth about interest rates, savings, and investment risk prepares them to achieve economic independence. Incorporating financial education into school curricula is a crucial step toward building a financially responsible society.

What is financial literacy according to the passage?
options: Ability to understand and use personal financial skills effectively
Earning high salary without planning expenses
Borrowing loans without understanding interest rates
Spending money on non-essential luxuries daily

questions.q: Passage 11 (Contd.): What is a direct consequence of lacking financial literacy?
options: Poor spending decisions and unmanageable debt

questions.q: Passage 11 (Contd.): What financial concepts should youth be educated about?
options: Interest rates, savings, and investment risk
How to take maximum credit card loans
Methods to spend income without budgeting

questions.q: Passage 11 (Contd.): What step is suggested to build a financially responsible society?
options: Incorporating financial education into school curricula
Restricting investments to real estate only

questions.q: Passage 11 (Contd.): What is the opposite of 'independence'?

Passage 12: Leadership is not merely about holding a title or exercising authority; it is about inspiring, guiding, and empowering others to achieve common goals. Effective leaders possess strong empathy, active listening skills, and clear integrity. They encourage innovation, foster a collaborative team environment, and take responsibility during failures. While management focuses on processes and structure, true leadership centers on people and vision.

According to the passage, what defines true leadership?
options: Inspiring, guiding, and empowering others toward common goals
Holding an official title and giving orders
Focusing exclusively on corporate rules and processes
Avoiding responsibility when team failures occur

questions.q: Passage 12 (Contd.): Which key trait is attributed to effective leaders in the text?
options: Disregard for team feedback and opinions

questions.q: Passage 12 (Contd.): How does leadership differ from management according to the text?
options: Leadership centers on people and vision, management on processes
Leadership deals with budgets, management with inspiration
Management is emotional, leadership is strictly structural
There is no difference between leadership and management

questions.q: Passage 12 (Contd.): What do effective leaders do when failures happen?
options: They take responsibility for the outcome
They ignore the issue and move forward
They resign from their position right away

questions.q: Passage 12 (Contd.): Choose the word that best defines 'integrity':

Passage 13: Mental health awareness has gained significant traction globally in recent years. Historically stigmatized, psychological well-being is now recognized as equally vital as physical health. Stress, anxiety, and depression can severely impair an individual's quality of life and workplace productivity if left unaddressed. Establishing accessible mental healthcare, promoting open conversations, and practicing stress reduction techniques are vital to creating a supportive social environment.

How has the global perception of mental health changed recently?
options: It is now recognized as equally vital as physical health
It is completely ignored in modern healthcare
It is treated as less important than physical illness
It is considered an unmanageable medical condition

questions.q: Passage 13 (Contd.): What impact can unaddressed mental health issues have?
options: Impair quality of life and workplace productivity

questions.q: Passage 13 (Contd.): What is required to build a supportive social environment for mental well-being?
options: Promoting open conversations and accessible care
Ignoring mental stress symptoms in schools
Restricting mental health treatments to hospitals

questions.q: Passage 13 (Contd.): Which conditions are specifically mentioned as damaging if left unaddressed?
options: Lack of physical agility and stamina

questions.q: Passage 13 (Contd.): Find the antonym of 'stigmatized':

Passage 14: Cultural heritage encompasses traditions, monuments, languages, and artistic expressions passed down through generations. Preserving cultural heritage fosters a sense of identity, social cohesion, and historical continuity among communities. In a rapidly globalizing world, indigenous languages and traditional art forms face the risk of extinction. Active preservation efforts, including museum documentation, cultural festivals, and educational integration, are necessary to safeguard this intangible wealth for future generations.

What does cultural heritage include according to the text?
options: Traditions, monuments, languages, and artistic expressions
Modern technological tools and gadgets only

questions.q: Passage 14 (Contd.): Why is preserving cultural heritage important for communities?
options: It fosters identity, social cohesion, and historical continuity

questions.q: Passage 14 (Contd.): What risk do indigenous languages face in a globalizing world?
options: Risk of replacing modern communication tools

questions.q: Passage 14 (Contd.): Which measure is suggested to safeguard cultural heritage?
options: Banning the speaking of local languages
Ignoring traditional art forms in schools

questions.q: Passage 14 (Contd.): What is the meaning of 'cohesion' as used in the passage?

Passage 15: Agriculture remains the backbone of developing economies, employing a substantial portion of the workforce and ensuring food security. However, smallholder farmers face severe challenges, including climate unpredictability, soil erosion, and lack of access to modern agricultural technology and capital. Implementing sustainable farming practices, such as crop rotation, organic fertilization, and micro-irrigation, can enhance yield while protecting soil health. Government support through subsidies, credit facilities, and crop insurance is vital to make small-scale farming viable.

Why is agriculture considered the backbone of developing economies?
options: It employs a large workforce and ensures food security
It relies completely on heavy urban industrial machinery
It eliminates the need for water resources
It generates no economic value for rural areas

questions.q: Passage 15 (Contd.): What major challenge do smallholder farmers confront?
options: Climate unpredictability and lack of modern technology

questions.q: Passage 15 (Contd.): Which sustainable farming practice is mentioned in the text?
Passage 15 (Contd.): How can governments assist small-scale farmers?
options: Through subsidies, credit facilities, and crop insurance
By imposing heavy taxes on farming equipment
By stopping credit availability to rural regions

questions.q: Passage 15 (Contd.): What is the synonym of 'viable' in the passage?

Passage 16: Urbanization has accelerated globally, leading to rapid growth of megacities. While urban areas serve as engines of economic growth and innovation, unplanned expansion creates severe infrastructure deficits. Slums, traffic congestion, inadequate waste management, and air pollution are frequent consequences of uncontrolled urban development. Sustainable urban planning requires investing in public mass transit, green spaces, affordable housing, and eco-friendly waste management systems to improve liveability.

What is a positive aspect of urban areas mentioned in the passage?
options: They serve as engines of economic growth and innovation
They reduce the demand for housing and infrastructure
They prevent atmospheric pollution in cities

questions.q: Passage 16 (Contd.): What negative consequence arises from unplanned urban expansion?
options: Traffic congestion and inadequate waste management
Abundance of public mass transit options

questions.q: Passage 16 (Contd.): What investment is crucial for sustainable urban planning?
options: Public mass transit, green spaces, and affordable housing
Expanding private vehicle usage on roads
Converting green parks into commercial concrete complexes
Reducing expenditure on waste processing facilities

questions.q: Passage 16 (Contd.): What is the main aim of sustainable urban planning?
options: To improve liveability in expanding cities

Passage 17: Scientific temperament is an attitude of mind that involves rational thinking, empirical observation, and questioning established dogmas. It encourages people to seek evidence before drawing conclusions and to remain open to revising opinions when presented with new facts. Promoting a scientific temper in society combats superstition, fatalism, and unscientific practices. Fostering curiosity and critical thinking in education systems is vital for nurturing this rational mindset.

What does possessing a scientific temperament involve?
options: Rational thinking, empirical observation, and questioning dogmas
Blindly accepting traditional beliefs without evidence
Rejecting all scientific discoveries and theories
Relying on fatalism to explain natural phenomena

questions.q: Passage 17 (Contd.): What does a person with scientific temper do when new facts emerge?
options: Remains open to revising existing opinions
Rejects new facts to protect old beliefs

questions.q: Passage 17 (Contd.): Promoting scientific temper helps combat which societal issue?
Passage 17 (Contd.): How can educational systems foster a scientific mindset?
options: By nurturing curiosity and critical thinking
By forcing rote memorization of facts

Passage 18: Gender equality is not only a fundamental human right but also a necessary foundation for a peaceful, prosperous, and sustainable world. Providing women and girls with equal access to education, healthcare, decent work, and representation in economic and political decision-making processes fuels sustainable economies. Despite progress, gender-based discrimination, wage gaps, and violence against women persist worldwide. Overcoming these barriers requires strong legal frameworks, policy enforcement, and socio-cultural shifts.

Why is gender equality essential according to the passage?
options: It is a fundamental human right and foundation for prosperity
It limits economic growth in developing countries
It restricts political participation to specific groups
It focuses exclusively on workplace wage adjustments

questions.q: Passage 18 (Contd.): What fuels sustainable economies according to the text?
options: Equal access to education, healthcare, and decision-making for women
Restricting employment opportunities for female workers
Ignoring female representation in political bodies

questions.q: Passage 18 (Contd.): Which persistent challenge is highlighted in the text?
Passage 18 (Contd.): What measures are needed to overcome barriers to gender equality?
options: Legal frameworks, policy enforcement, and socio-cultural shifts
Reducing women's access to higher education
Discouraging open discussions on equal rights

questions.q: Passage 18 (Contd.): What is the meaning of 'persist' in the passage?

Passage 19: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming industries ranging from healthcare and finance to transportation and education. Machine learning algorithms analyze vast amounts of data to identify patterns, make predictions, and automate complex tasks with high accuracy. While AI offers immense potential for economic growth and scientific discovery, it raises ethical concerns regarding job displacement, algorithmic bias, and data privacy. Developing robust regulatory frameworks is essential to ensure AI benefits humanity safely and equitably.

How do machine learning algorithms process information?
options: By analyzing vast data to identify patterns and make predictions
By relying solely on human manual data entry
By ignoring statistical patterns in datasets
By making random guesses without analytical data

questions.q: Passage 19 (Contd.): Which field is mentioned as being transformed by AI?
Passage 19 (Contd.): What ethical concern is associated with the advancement of AI?
options: Lack of interest from technology developers

questions.q: Passage 19 (Contd.): What is required to ensure AI benefits humanity safely?
options: Allowing unmonitored deployment of AI tools

questions.q: Passage 19 (Contd.): Choose the word that means 'equitably':

Passage 20: Microplastics—tiny plastic particles less than five millimeters in length—have become a ubiquitous contaminant in marine and terrestrial environments. Originating from fragmented plastic waste, synthetic textiles, and industrial processes, these particles accumulate in food chains, posing toxic risks to marine organisms and human health. Standard water filtration systems often fail to capture microplastics due to their minuscule size. Addressing this crisis requires reducing single-use plastics, upgrading wastewater treatment infrastructure, and developing biodegradable alternative materials.

What are microplastics defined as?
options: Plastic particles less than five millimeters in length
Large plastic bags floating on ocean surfaces
Chemical solvents used in water treatment

questions.q: Passage 20 (Contd.): Why do standard water filtration systems struggle to remove microplastics?
options: Because microplastics dissolve in water instantly
Because filtration plants refuse to filter them
Due to their heavy weight and density

questions.q: Passage 20 (Contd.): What danger do microplastics present when they accumulate in food chains?
options: Toxic risks to marine organisms and human health
Increased nutrient richness in sea water

questions.q: Passage 20 (Contd.): Which solution is proposed to tackle microplastic pollution?
options: Increasing the production of synthetic textiles
Dumping plastic waste exclusively in terrestrial landfills

questions.q: Passage 20 (Contd.): What does 'ubiquitous' mean in the passage context?
